title: 3Sum Closest
summary: You get a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`. Pick three numbers at three different positions so that their sum is as close as possible to `target`, and return that sum, not the numbers. Exactly one sum is closest, so the answer is unique.

examples.explanation: 3 + (-8) + 5 = 0 is 1 away from the target, and no three numbers add up to 1 or 2.
No sum reaches 20, so the largest one, 8 + 1 + 4 = 13, comes closest.

constraints: nums is in no particular order

approaches.twist: Sort, fix one number, run two pointers on the rest, and keep the sum nearest to target.

signals.meaning: Fix one number and the other two become a pair: run two pointers on the rest of the sorted list, once per fixed number.
No exact hit is promised, so remember the closest sum so far. Start the best distance at float('inf') so the first sum always replaces it.
Only the sum is returned, not positions, so you're free to sort first. Sorting costs O(n log n), cheap next to the O(n²) search, and it lets each pointer move push the sum up or down.

constraintReading: len(nums) is at most 500, so checking every triple means about 2·10⁷ sums (O(n³)), slow in Python, while O(n²) is at most 2.5·10⁵ steps. That allows one fixed number plus one inward pass for the other two. Sorting first adds only O(n log n), and sorting in place keeps the extra space O(1).

related.relation: Same sort, fixed number and two pointers, but it collects every triple that sums to exactly zero and skips duplicates instead of keeping the nearest sum.
